name: Reuben Szymański-Okafor
creator: Reuben Szymański-Okafor
description: For eleven years, Szymański-Okafor was the most productive ghostwriter in the GLMZ publishing ecosystem, producing authorized biographies, corporate histories, and Tier 4-5 memoir content under seventeen different client names. When he surfaced publicly in 2214 and published 'Everything I Wrote for Them,' a memoir-cum-exposé that reproduced verbatim passages from sealed corporate documents he had been hired to narrativize, the legal fallout was immediate and ongoing. The book's central argument — that corponation narrative management is itself a form of weapons manufacture — made him simultaneously celebrated and radioactive.
medium: neural feed and physical hardprint (legal injunctions have suppressed three editions)
cultural_impact: His exposé revealed that at least four prominent 'Tier 5 memoirists' were entirely his invention — the named authors had provided only broad parameters. This destabilized the premium memoir market and caused a brief but genuine crisis of authenticity in Spire literary circles.
controversy: Seven separate corponation legal actions are currently active against him. Two of the 'authors' whose identities he fabricated have sued for defamation. He maintains that the defamation claim is impossible since the 'authors' did not exist to be defamed — this argument is currently before a corporate arbitration panel.
story_hooks: Szymański-Okafor approaches the players with evidence of a ghostwritten document that, if authenticated, would implicate a Tier 5 family in a Shelf displacement operation.
One of his fabricated 'authors' has begun publicly performing the identity he created for them — and seems to believe they are that person.
He claims his most damaging files were stolen before he could publish them and wants help recovering them from a corporate data vault.
